text:
Emma: FYI multiple Dedicated tenants in ap-east1 reporting sharp p95 latency increases and intermittent placement errors. Reports started ~10:20 UTC.
Zoe (CS): we have live tickets from 3 tenants on pool ap-east1-pool-3. Symptoms: 429s, occasional 503 placement failures. sample req id r-0a3b9c2f from tenant A.
InfraBot: [alert] ap-east1-pool-3 GPU allocation contention detected (2026-11-05T10:21:30Z). autoscaler: scale_down blocked by pod constraints.
Miguel (eng-oncall): paste router placement error logs and run `/infra check-pool ap-east1 pool-3 --diag`. Need exact failure details.
Raj: router grep (truncated):
```
ERROR placement: failed to allocate slot: reason=overcommit, details=\"no GPU available for model x-large, requested 4gpus\"
WARN throttle: backoff=120s active=17
```
Zoe (CS): repro we used with tenant B: 1) open 8 concurrent sessions pinned to model x-large 2) each session uses batch=8, seq=2048 3) after ~2-3m placement retries and 429s observed.
Julia (SRE): node metrics show several GPUs at ~98% memory. One tenant (tenant-42) has ~40 long-lived pinned sessions holding KV caches. Looks like cross-tenant noisy neighbor causing fragmentation.
Miguel (eng-oncall): that matches noisy-tenant pattern. Options: evict/migrate tenant-42, enable tenant isolation, or route affected tenants to another region. What can infra do without violating dedicated customer constraints?
Raj: tried soft affinity moves but containers are pinned; infra policy prevents live eviction for dedicated customers without consent.
Emma: observability snapshot: p95 latency spike graph -> https://console.redwood/obs/ap-east1/pool-3?range=15m. Scheduling latency rising, GPU memory saturated, CPU idle.
Zoe (CS): customers pushing for mitigation--they can't tolerate sustained 5-8s p95.
Miguel (eng-oncall): short-term mitigations we can run now:
- enable cross-region failover for consenting tenants (route to ap-southeast-1) — tradeoff: higher network latency for some end-users
- temporarily increase autoscaler max for pool-3 if customer contract allows and capacity exists
- contact noisy tenant to reduce pinned sessions or move to reserved nodes
Julia (SRE): autoscaler logs show scale_up denied due to project quota: `scale_up denied: reason=quota_limit_project, requested_gpus=16, available=0`. So on-demand GPU cold pool in ap-east1 is exhausted.
Raj: confirmed regional stockout for on-demand GPUs. Capacity team ETA for replenishment ~6 hours.
Julia (SRE): propose a degraded throttling policy: cap concurrent sessions per-tenant to 12 and enforce max batch-size=4 to reduce memory pressure.
Miguel (eng-oncall): implemented per-tenant temporary caps for affected tenant IDs and pushed config. Rolling now.
Zoe (CS): CS notified tenants A/B/C: tenant B accepted cross-region failover; tenant A opted to try caps first. Providing repro and timeline.
Emma: added repro snippet for runbook:
```
# quick repro (do not run against production tenants)
for i in {1..8}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood/v1/generate -d '{"model":"x-large","seq":2048}' &
done
```
Miguel (eng-oncall): next steps: 1) open capacity escalation with partners (ticket CP-7643 opened), 2) send CS ETA, 3) prepare automatic tenant isolation rule to trigger if stockout persists >30m.
InfraBot: ticket CP-7643 created (ap-east1 on-demand shortage), owner @Capacity Lead.
Raj: adding this thread to incidents board and will retest in 30m after caps applied.
Emma: monitoring update ~10:38 UTC: p95 dropped from ~6s to ~2.1s after caps. Keeping watch.
Zoe (CS): updated customers with current status; will reopen thread if regressions occur.
